sampling_model.design: An i.i.d. randomized experiment with fixed finite stratum set \(\mathcal J\), fixed finite action set \(\mathcal A\), and known action probabilities \(e_{ja}\).
sampling_model.units: For each local row \(n\), the full units \(O_{n1},\ldots,O_{nn}\) are i.i.d. from \(P_n\), while the planner observes only \(O^{\mathrm{obs}}_{ni}=(X_{ni},A_{ni},Y_{ni})\) and hence only \(\mathcal F_n^{\mathrm{obs}}\).
sampling_model.treatment: Conditional randomization satisfies \(Y^{\mathrm{pot}}\perp A\mid X\), consistency, and \(e_{ja}\ge e_{\min}\).
sampling_model.overlap: Every stratum has \(p_j\ge p_{\min}\), every randomized action has \(e_{ja}\ge e_{\min}\), and every benchmark action has \(b_{ja}\ge\beta\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Finite randomized cells are estimated by within-cell Hájek means and stratum masses by empirical frequencies. These observed estimators generate \(\widehat{\mathfrak F}_n\), the only frontier supplied to the temperature selector. The Gaussian approximation envelope for the distinct oracle regret path is derived from bounded outcomes, cell mass, and overlap in \(\mathrm{lem:cell\mbox{-}gaussian}\), rather than assumed for the estimator.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: For fixed positive \(\lambda\), \(nR_\lambda(\widehat\theta)\) converges to one-half of a Gaussian quadratic form; the surrounding randomized model includes the binary witness used here.
A predetermined diverging inverse temperature yields root-\(n\) asymptotic linearity for the unsmoothed optimal-policy value.
Convergent binary treatment rules are represented by rules in a shifted Gaussian limit experiment.
A scalar empirical-process supremum is coupled nonasymptotically to the corresponding Gaussian supremum.
The concentration function of a standardized Gaussian-process supremum is bounded by its expected supremum.
Ordinary bootstrap consistency under a Gaussian limit is equivalent to full differentiability of the transformation.
Gaussian-vector maxima admit covariance comparison and anti-concentration bounds under arbitrary correlation.
A separation-of-variables transformation reduces Gaussian rectangle probabilities to bounded multiple integration.
Taylor expansion, interval analysis, and automatic differentiation self-validate Gaussian rectangle probabilities.
Recursive integration evaluates noncentered Gaussian orthant probabilities for positive-definite correlation matrices.
Joint Gaussian critical values give coverage after selecting a series dimension from the searched specification set.

body.tldr: On a declared fixed finite-cell randomized causal subclass, benchmark-centered Gibbs rules form one compact continuous regret path with hard-lottery and projected-quadratic endpoints. The note proves a quantitative uniform Gaussian approximation and a terminating, machine-checkable one-sided calibration that remains valid after every observed-data-measurable temperature choice and at quantile atoms. The positive path law and calibration are not extended to the full Fang--Ridder--Xie model class. In the converse direction, an exact cellwise atom formula and a legal two-stratum binary collision witness rule out a uniform atom-removed small-interval modulus; because that witness satisfies the published class's randomization, overlap, boundedness, and positive-benchmark hypotheses, this negative conclusion transfers upward to the broader class.

project_justification.gap: Fixed positive KL penalties have a quadratic regret law, while hard assignment and predetermined softmax sequences are studied separately. No published result supplies a quantitative joint path law or a certified atom-safe critical value over the full penalty menu. Standard Gaussian-supremum anti-concentration also cannot handle the colliding hard-cell atoms exhibited here, including within the broader Fang--Ridder--Xie class.
project_justification.niche: For fixed finite strata and actions, the lottery problem becomes a tractable but nonstandard function-valued statistic with nonlinear Gaussian interior coordinates, benchmark-weighted multiway ties, and a quadratic opposite endpoint. The same finite subclass is rich enough to expose positive-mass hard-cell atoms whose levels collide, so it supports both computable positive inference and an upward-transfer impossibility result.
project_justification.fill: The project proves the finite-cell Gaussian path approximation, both endpoint limits, the selection bridge, and a terminating lower-CDF certificate with an analytic fallback. It also proves the exact atom formula and a fixed legal counterexample to uniform atom-removed anti-concentration. Positive achievability remains confined to the declared finite-cell class; only the negative conclusion transfers to the broader Fang--Ridder--Xie class that contains the witness.

body.related_work: Fang--Ridder--Xie proves a quadratic regret limit for each fixed positive penalty in a broader randomized assignment model and leaves data-driven penalty choice open. The present positive path law and certified calibration require the narrower declared fixed finite-cell subclass and are not extensions over the full published class. The relation is asymmetric: the two-stratum binary counterexample satisfies Fang--Ridder--Xie's randomization, overlap, boundedness, and positive-benchmark hypotheses, so the failure of uniform atom-removed anti-concentration transfers upward. Whitehouse--Chen--Austern--Syrgkanis studies one predetermined diverging smoother for a different scalar target. Hirano--Porter supplies a binary shifted-Gaussian local decision experiment. Chernozhukov--Chetverikov--Kato and Giessing treat Gaussian-process suprema, whereas the present supremum is nonlinear and has colliding hard-cell atoms. Fang--Santos studies directional irregularity; Genz, Wang--Kennedy, and Miwa--Hayter--Kuriki supply Gaussian integration components; and Kang supplies simultaneous-band selection logic. None yields the atom-safe continuum certificate proved on the declared subclass here.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The work-capped algorithm always terminates because it can issue an analytic Gaussian-tail fallback, and its one-sided lower-CDF certificate remains valid at atoms. It need not approximate the ideal least-favorable critical value within a prescribed numerical width. Colliding positive-mass atoms prove that the missing uniform atom-removed modulus cannot be recovered from the declared assumptions or from the broader Fang--Ridder--Xie hypotheses containing the witness. A two-sided value-width guarantee therefore needs an additional separation, restricted-state, or explicit atom-structure condition; the positive path law itself remains confined to the finite-cell subclass.
body.honest_scope: Positive uniform approximation and calibration are claimed only for fixed finite strata and actions, known randomized propensities, positive benchmark probabilities, positive cell masses, bounded outcomes, compact local contrasts, root-sample-size localization, and a supplied covariance spectrum bounded away from zero. They are not claimed for the full Fang--Ridder--Xie class, boundary benchmarks, singular covariance, growing dimension, disappearing cells, or continuous covariates without prespecified finite stratification. The commitment-savings display is conditional on such cells. The upward class transfer applies only to the negative result: the binary witness lies in the broader published class, so that class cannot support the rejected uniform modulus or a probability-to-critical-value conversion based on it.
body.interpretation: The positive result is deliberately one-sided and deliberately subclass-specific: within fixed finite randomized cells, one auditable critical value covers the entire normalized oracle-regret path and therefore every measurable temperature choice. The negative result has broader reach. Nearby local states retain positive atoms at hard-cell levels that approach one another, so no vanishing atom-removed modulus, and hence no conversion based on one, can hold uniformly over any larger model class containing this witness, including the Fang--Ridder--Xie class.
